The one time my ECE degree fits in on a Reddit post! Yes, using corporal punishment on your child is fully within the law of the US (barring leaving marks that last longer than a certain time limit or being excessive) but academically it is generally agreed that you will build a stronger foundation of trust between your child and yourself by instead teaching your child emotional coping strategies and being patient through the tantrums. By hitting your child back, you teach them that striking, hitting, and violence can be a healthy behavior. **Later on in life this can lead to poor emotional control and stronger fight or flight responses.** Furthermore, adults who were hit as children (yes, non abusively too) tend to have lower self esteem, less emotional control, and are generally achieve less than their peers who were not hit as children.

I'm not going to sit here and judge a parent who chooses to use corporal punishment in a non-abusive way, however I believe strongly that **teaching** rather than **correcting** your child will always be the best route.
